paragraphs:
Rav Seḥora. Rava praised him to Rav Naḥman as a great man; he asked to meet him. Seḥora needed release from a vow. R. Naḥman repeatedly asked whether he had vowed anticipating a particular circumstance; each time he answered yes. Angered, R. Naḥman sent him to his lodging, unable to find an opening. Rav Seḥora went out and found his own: the proper path brings credit from others, etc.; he had not vowed anticipating R. Naḥman's anger. He released it for himself, Nedarim 22b.

It says Rav Seḥora illuminated one Mishnah for Rabbah, who tore his clothes at Seḥora's death. This is mistaken. Bava Metzia 33a: if one's father and teacher bear burdens, relieve the teacher first. R. Meir defines teacher as one who taught wisdom, not Scripture or Mishnah; R. Yehudah, one from whom most wisdom came; R. Yose, even one who illuminated one Mishnah. Rava gives Rav Seḥora, who explained zohama listron. Rashi: a large spoon used to move pot/scalding-pan scum aside, a utensil in Tohorot whose identity Rava had not known. Shemuel tore his clothes for a rabbi who explained 'one reaches down as far as the armpit, and the other opens it straightaway'—a Mishnah in Tamid. He inferred Rava too tore his clothes because Shemuel's case follows, but read and erred.

Moreover, Rav Seḥora was Rava's principal teacher. Tosafot Avodah Zarah 19a: Rava reports Rav Seḥora reporting Rav Huna. Numerous reports show he was principal teacher: Berakhot 5a, 26a; Shabbat 24a; Sanhedrin 49b; Yevamot 106a; Menaḥot 40b; Bava Kamma 21a reports Rav Huna. At the end of Elu Metzi'ot some read Rabbah and some Rava; he means that even had he received only this relatively unnovel explanation, he would be obliged to tear his clothes. End of Tosafot. Likewise Tosafot Yevamot 106a. At the beginning of Dinei Mamonot 49b, Tosafot explains: Rav Seḥora personally taught him only that; elsewhere he transmitted Rav Huna. Alternatively, even only this would establish teacherhood; or at that time Rava had not learned more. End of quotation.

Thus Rava learned much from Rav Seḥora; why say he tore clothes for only zohama listron, when no tearing by Rava is stated at all? A thousand pardons from the holy Tosafists: Avodah Zarah and Yevamot 106 say Rava would have to tear clothes even for one teaching, but the passage concerns the Mishnah's teacher-honor precedence over one's father, not tearing. Tosafot Dinei Mamonot itself says even one teaching establishes a teacher. Furthermore, Tosafot carefully says Rava ought to tear, not that he did, as Yuḥasin understood. Eruvin 54b has Rabbah—Ein Yaakov, Rava—report Rav Seḥora reporting Rav Huna. Rabbah is a scribal error: the same matter in Avodah Zarah 19 has Rava. For burial see R. Abba bar Yehudah.
